title: Transplant status and rejection
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's transplant status or transplant complication only.
note:
Chief Complaint
Routine follow-up for stable status.

HPI
The patient is a 68-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding his history of a small bowel transplant performed several years ago. He reports feeling well overall and denies any abdominal pain, diarrhea, or significant weight changes. He maintains a good nutritional status and reports that his appetite remains consistent. He currently feels stable on his existing immunosuppressive regimen. There are no signs or symptoms of organ rejection at this time.

Medication List
Tacrolimus, Mycophenolate mofetil, Prednisone.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. He appears healthy and well-nourished. Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and non-tender to palpation. Bowel sounds are present in all four quadrants. Vital signs are stable and within normal limits.

Assessment
The patient is a 68-year-old male who is stable following his small bowel transplant. He is tolerating his medications well with no evidence of rejection and maintains excellent nutritional status.

Plan
Continue current immunosuppressive medications as prescribed. Follow up in three months for routine monitoring.

Electronically signed,
K. Nguyen, PA-C
